First, intro: Maltese dogs have long, silky, hypoallergenic coats that require gentle, regular care to stay mat-free and shiny; this step-by-step guide covers the full bathing and drying process, with product and tool recommendations to make the routine efficient and effective.
Then 10 steps: Let's outline them:
1. Gather all required products and tools first to avoid leaving your dog unattended mid-process: Products include pH-balanced hypoallergenic dog shampoo (preferably whitening or moisturizing formulated for light coats, avoid human shampoos), leave-in or rinse-out conditioner designed for long-haired breeds, detangling spray, and optional coat oil for extra shine. Tools you'll need: slicker brush (soft or medium bristle), stainless steel metal comb (wide and narrow tooth), absorbent microfiber towels, high-velocity low-heat pet blow dryer, non-slip bath mat, and detangler spray.
2. Pre-brush the entire coat thoroughly before bathing to remove existing mats, tangles, and loose fur, working in 1-inch sections from the skin outward to avoid pulling; this takes 10-15 minutes and prevents mats from tightening when wet.
3. Prepare the bathing area: Fill a bathtub or sink with 2-3 inches of lukewarm (not hot, around 100°F/38°C) water, place a non-slip mat on the bottom to keep your Maltese steady, and have all products within arm's reach.
4. Wet your dog's coat completely from the neck down, avoiding getting water directly in their ears and eyes; use a handheld shower head or cup for gentle, controlled pouring, and make sure the coat is saturated all the way to the skin.
5. Apply a small amount of the pH-balanced Maltese-specific or light-coat dog shampoo to your hands, lather it gently, and work it into the coat in the direction of hair growth, massaging carefully into the skin without scrubbing roughly to avoid tangling; pay extra attention to dirt-prone areas like the paws, belly, and around the mouth.
6. Rinse the shampoo completely from the coat with lukewarm water, running your fingers through the fur to ensure no soap residue remains, as leftover shampoo can cause skin irritation and dull the coat; rinsing typically takes 3-5 minutes for a full coat.
7. Apply a long-hair dog conditioner evenly throughout the coat, avoiding the root area if your Maltese has particularly fine hair to prevent greasiness; let it sit for 2-3 minutes as directed on the product label to soften the fur and reduce tangling.
8. Rinse the conditioner thoroughly (unless using a leave-in formula), then gently squeeze excess water from the coat with your hands, followed by patting dry with absorbent microfiber towels; avoid rubbing the coat vigorously, as this causes frizz and tangles.
9. Use a low-heat, high-velocity pet blow dryer (set to the lowest heat setting to avoid burning sensitive skin) to dry the coat completely, working in 1-inch sections while brushing through with a slicker brush simultaneously in the direction of hair growth; hold the dryer 6-8 inches away from the skin, and continue until every layer of fur is fully dry, as damp fur is prone to matting.
10. Finish by running a dual-sided stainless steel comb through the entire coat to catch any remaining tangles, then spritz with a light detangling spray to prevent future mats; double-check hard-to-reach areas like behind the ears, under the legs, and at the base of the tail for any missed knots.
Then time estimate: The entire process typically takes 45 to 75 minutes total, depending on coat length, how many mats are present pre-bath, and how much experience you have with the routine.
Conclusion: Following this routine regularly (every 1-2 weeks for full-groomed Maltese) will keep their coat soft, shiny, and completely free of painful mats and tangles between grooming sessions.

Maltese dogs have long, silky, hypoallergenic coats that require gentle, regular care to stay mat-free, shiny, and healthy; this step-by-step guide covers the full bathing and drying process, with product and tool recommendations to make the routine efficient and low-stress for both you and your dog.

1. Gather all required products and tools first to avoid leaving your dog unattended mid-process: Recommended products include pH-balanced hypoallergenic dog shampoo (preferably whitening or moisturizing formulated for light, long coats, never use human shampoos which disrupt canine skin pH), rinse-out or leave-in conditioner designed for long-haired small breeds, lightweight detangling spray, and optional argan coat oil for extra shine. Tools you will need: soft/medium bristle slicker brush, dual-sided stainless steel metal comb (wide and narrow tooth), 2-3 absorbent microfiber towels, low-heat high-velocity pet blow dryer, non-slip bath mat, and cotton balls to place in ears to keep water out.
2. Pre-brush the entire coat thoroughly before bathing to remove existing mats, tangles, and loose fur, working in 1-inch sections from the skin outward to avoid pulling on sensitive skin; this takes 10-15 minutes and prevents existing mats from tightening and becoming impossible to remove once wet.
3. Prepare the bathing area: Fill a bathtub or sink with 2-3 inches of lukewarm water (around 100°F/38°C, test with your wrist to ensure it is not too hot), place a non-slip mat on the bottom to keep your Maltese steady, and tuck a small cotton ball in each ear to prevent water from entering the ear canal.
4. Wet your dog's coat completely from the neck down, avoiding getting water directly in their eyes; use a handheld shower head or plastic cup for gentle, controlled pouring, and make sure the coat is saturated all the way to the skin, not just the outer layer of fur.
5. Apply a small amount of the pH-balanced light-coat dog shampoo to your palms, lather it gently between your hands, and work it into the coat in the direction of hair growth, massaging carefully into the skin without scrubbing roughly to avoid tangling; pay extra attention to dirt-prone areas like the paws, belly, and around the mouth where food and saliva staining often occurs.
6. Rinse the shampoo completely from the coat with lukewarm water, running your fingers through the fur to ensure no soap residue remains, as leftover shampoo can cause skin irritation, itchiness, and dull the coat; rinsing typically takes 3-5 minutes for a full length Maltese coat.
7. Apply a long-hair dog conditioner evenly throughout the coat, avoiding the root area if your Maltese has particularly fine hair to prevent greasiness at the scalp; let it sit for 2-3 minutes as directed on the product label to soften the fur and reduce tangling during drying.
8. Rinse the conditioner thoroughly if using a rinse-out formula (skip this step for leave-in conditioner), then gently squeeze excess water from the coat with your hands, followed by patting dry with absorbent microfiber towels; avoid rubbing the coat vigorously, as this causes frizz, breakage, and new tangles.
9. Use a low-heat, high-velocity pet blow dryer (set to the lowest heat setting to avoid burning your Maltese's sensitive skin) to dry the coat completely, working in 1-inch sections while brushing through with a slicker brush simultaneously in the direction of hair growth; hold the dryer 6-8 inches away from the skin, and continue until every layer of fur is fully dry, as even slightly damp fur is highly prone to matting within hours of grooming.
10. Finish by running a dual-sided stainless steel comb through the entire coat to catch any remaining tangles, then spritz with a light detangling spray to prevent future mats; double-check hard-to-reach areas like behind the ears, under the legs, and at the base of the tail for any missed knots you did not catch during drying.

The entire process typically takes 45 to 75 minutes total, depending on coat length, how many mats are present pre-bath, and how much experience you have with the routine. Following this routine every 1-2 weeks will keep your Maltese's coat soft, shiny, and completely free of painful mats and tangles between full grooming sessions.
